B2L01-G01-P30: Put 一下 after a verb to say the action is short or small.
It is often used for requests, asking for help politely, or making an action sound relaxed.
An object can come after 一下: 看一下菜單.
一下 is about a short, light action, while 一次 counts how many times.
B2L01-G02-P31: Put 最好 before a verb to give advice about what someone should do, like 最好休息.
For advice not to do something, use 最好不要.
Here 最好 gives advice and doesn't mean the best one. A noun can't follow it.
B2L01-G03-P32: 不但……也…… says two things are both true.
If both parts share one subject, put 不但 after the subject, not before it.
Put 也 right before the second point.
If the parts describe different sides of one topic, put 也 before the second side: 風景美，交通也很方便.
B2L01-G04-P32: Put 完 right after a verb to show the action is finished.
Say V完了 for done and 還沒V完 for not finished yet.
完 says the action is all done. 了 only shows something is complete or has changed.
Put 了 at the end, after 完: 吃完飯了, not 吃了完飯.
B2L01-G05-P38: Put 在 after the verb and before the place to say where a person or thing ends up.
Common verbs here are 住, 坐 and 站. 放 is used too.
Pick a verb that fits: 住在 is for living, while things use 放在 or 寫在.
In this pattern 在 comes after the verb. You can't say 在坐.
B2L01-G06-P38: Put 給 after a verb and before the receiver to show who gets the thing.
Common ones are 送給, 賣給, 寄給, 拿給, 帶給 and 寫給.
給 must come right after a verb, and the receiver comes after 給: 寄給媽媽.
B2L01-G07-P39: Use 一邊 before each of two actions to say they happen at the same time, not one after the other.
It usually goes with specific action verbs.
One person can do both actions, or two people can each do one.
With one person, you can leave out 一 on both sides. With two people, keep 一.
B2L01-G08-P40: 雖然 admits a fact, then 可是 gives something unexpected or opposite.
Both the 雖然 part and the 可是 part must appear, and 可是 carries the contrast.
Don't use 所以 here, because 可是 shows contrast while 所以 shows a result.
Use 可是 or 但是 for the second part. 也 only adds and doesn't show contrast.
B2L01-G09-P41: Put 呢 at the end of a statement to stress an action or fact in a polite, relaxed tone.
This is not the 呢 of a question. For yes or no questions use 嗎.
吧 means a guess or suggestion. 呢 stresses a fact and sounds more sure.
B2L02-G01-P51: 把 puts the thing you act on before the verb and says what was done to it.
The verb must act on the object, like 看, 吃, 賣 or 寫.
The verb needs a result after it, such as 了 or 完. Plain 吃 isn't enough.
Put 不, 沒 or 別 before 把.
B2L02-G02-P51: Use 完 in a 把 sentence to say an action on the object is finished: 把家事做完.
完 goes right after the verb.
我完了 is different: it means all hope is gone, while 做完 means the action ended.
B2L02-G03-P52: Use V一V in a 把 sentence for a quick, light action on the object.
It makes a request or instruction sound more polite and relaxed.
Only use one-syllable verbs, like 洗一洗 or 掃一掃.
B2L02-G04-P53: Put 給 after the verb in a 把 sentence to say who receives the object.
Say the thing first, then the verb with 給, then the receiver: 把舊車賣給你.
Don't put 給 before the verb. Common verbs are 送, 賣, 拿 and 寄.
B2L02-G05-P54: Put 多 before 大, 長, 高 or 遠 to ask how big, long, tall or far something is.
多 goes before the word: say 多高, not 高多.
有 can come before 多 but is often left out: 有多遠 or 多遠.
B2L02-G06-P54: Put a length of time before 沒 or 不 to say how long an action hasn't happened: 兩天沒睡覺.
了 often comes at the end. With 沒, it shows the state still continues up to now.
不 can describe a repeated or habitual absence of the action.
多久沒 asks how long since the last time, not how many times.
B2L02-G07-P55: Put 都 or 也 after a question word to mean everything, everyone or everywhere.
In a positive sentence it includes all. In a negative sentence it means none.
The question word comes first, then 都 or 也: 誰也不認識.
B2L02-G08-P56: 又 says the same action or a similar situation happens again.
又 goes before the verb and often pairs with 了 or 沒.
再 is for wanting or planning to do it again, usually after a word like can or want.
B2L02-G09-P56: Put 才 before the verb to say something happens later than expected, which the speaker sees as late.
The time comes first, then 才, then the verb: 十一點才起來.
B2L02-G10-P62: Put 在 or 到 and the place after the verb in a 把 sentence, not before it: 丟在浴室裡.
在 marks where the object stays after the action. 到 marks the place it reaches.
An address stays on the envelope, so use 寫在. Use 寄到 for sending something to a place.
B2L02-G11-P63: 才 goes in the second part and says the result happens only after the earlier condition or reason is true.
Put 才 right before the result: 才不會覺得冷.
The first part often has 得, 要, 為了 or 因為.
B2L03-G01-P75: 來 means toward the speaker, and 去 means away from the speaker.
A direction word plus 來 or 去 gives the direction of the move, like 上來 or 下去.
Choose by where the speaker is. Speaking from upstairs, say 請上來.
起來 is a fixed phrase meaning up. There is no 起去.
B2L03-G02-P77: Put a motion verb first, then a direction word and 來 or 去, to say which way something moves.
Motion verbs here include 走, 跑, 帶, 放, 拿, 搬 and 站.
Say the action first, then the direction: 走出來, not 出來走.
Things moving away from the speaker take 去, like 帶回去.
B2L03-G03-P78: To say where something ends up, add the place after the direction word and before 來 or 去.
The order is motion verb, direction word, place, then 來 or 去: 帶回日本去, not 帶回去日本.
B2L03-G04-P79: After 把 put the thing being moved, then the motion verb, the direction word and 來 or 去.
You can add a place before 來 or 去: 把衣服拿上樓去.
Don't stop at the motion verb. Add a direction word after it.
Put 了 last, after 來 or 去, to show it is done.
B2L03-G05-P79: Repeat a two-syllable verb as XYXY to say you do the action briefly and casually.
Don't add 一下 or 一點 to it. XYXY already means a short time.
Don't put 一 in the middle: say 打掃打掃, not 打掃一打掃.
B2L03-G06-P80: Verb plus 起來 gives your feeling or opinion about a person or thing.
The verb is often one syllable, such as 看, 聽, 吃, 喝 or 穿.
Put the comment last, after 起來: 看起來不錯.
For how clothes look on you, use 穿起來.
B2L03-G07-P81: 替 means doing something in place of someone who can't do it themselves.
Put 替 and the person before the verb: 替我裝網路.
Always say what is done. You can't stop after 替他.
B2L03-G08-P86: Say one thing first, then add another, more important thing.
After 除了 you can use a noun, a verb, or a short sentence.
Put 還 before the second verb or adjective.
If the two parts have different subjects, the second subject goes before 還.
B2L03-G09-P87: Use 把 and an action verb plus 得 to say how far or how well the action turned out.
The thing being handled goes right after 把.
Put 得 right after the verb, then the degree or result: 把足球踢得很遠.
B2L04-G01-P99: Use 就 before 在 or 是 to say it is right here, or exactly this one.
Don't use 才 for this. 才 means late, slow, or only that much.
When someone asks who is there or if you are home, answer 我就是, not 我就在.
B2L04-G02-P100: 到 after a verb means the action reached its result.
V到了 and 沒V到 say whether the action worked in the end.
V得到 and V不到 say whether you have the ability or the chance to do it.
Put 不 between the verb and 到: 找不到, not 不到找.
B2L04-G03-P101: 懂 after a verb means you understood, often after 聽 or 看.
V懂了 and 沒V懂 say whether you understood in the end. 沒看懂 means you looked but didn't understand.
V得懂 and V不懂 say whether you are able to understand. 看不懂 is for something too hard for you.
Put 懂 after the verb: 聽懂, not 懂聽.
B2L04-G04-P108: Put 得不得了 or 極了 after a state word to say the degree is very high.
Don't put 很 or 非常 before the word. You can't say 很累得不得了.
B2L04-G05-P110: 越來越 says a degree or amount keeps getting bigger or smaller over time.
Put it after the subject and before the verb or adjective: 朋友越來越少了.
B2L04-G06-P111: V得起 and V不起 say whether you can afford something.
It is used with only a few verbs, such as 吃, 喝, 買, 住 and 租.
You can't say V起了 or 沒V起. Say 買不起, not 沒買起.
B2L04-G07-P112: 飽 after a verb means you have had enough, as in 吃飽 and 睡飽.
V飽了 and 沒V飽 say whether you got enough in the end.
V得飽 and V不飽 say whether you are able to get enough.
Put 飽 right after the verb: 睡飽了, not 睡了飽.
B2L04-G08-P113: Use 對 and the thing, then 有興趣, to say you are interested in someone or something.
Always use 對 for the thing, not 在.
Put 興趣 after 有 or 沒有. A degree word can go before 有: 很有興趣.
B2L05-G01-P122: 被 makes a sentence where the subject gets the action. After the verb, say the result.
The doer can go after 被, or be left out.
Put 沒 before 被, not before the verb.
Don't swap 被 and 把. With 把 the subject does the action. With 被 it receives the action.
B2L05-G02-P123: V著V著 says that while one action goes on, something else happens.
The second part often has 就 and ends with 了.
If the second part has its own subject, put it before 就, not after.
It is not V一V: 聊一聊 just means to chat a little.
B2L05-G03-P124: 只要 gives a condition that is enough, and 就 gives the result.
Use 就 for the result, not 才. 才 means the condition is hard or the result comes late.
It is not the same as 要是, which only gives an if-situation.
B2L05-G04-P124: 有時候 goes before two actions or situations to say how often each one happens.
Put 有時候 before the verb, and use it twice.
The two parts can be different actions, or one action with different things.
B2L05-G05-P130: 起來 after a verb or state word says the action or state starts and keeps going.
At the end of a sentence, it can also show a result.
With an object, put the object between 起 and 來: 下起雨來.
To say something starts to get lively, use 起來, not 極了. 極了 means the highest degree.
B2L05-G06-P130: 還好 says something good happened. 要不然 says what bad thing could have happened otherwise.
Put the good situation after 還好 and the bad result after 要不然.
Don't use 但是 here. It only shows contrast, not relief.
B2L05-G07-P131: Say how often something happens: 每, a time unit, the action, then the number of times.
Put the number of times after the verb: 考一次, not before it.
Put 每 before the amount: 每三天.
Add 就 to show it happens even more often.
B2L05-G08-P132: A像B一樣 says A is like B.
Put the way they are alike after 一樣: 像蘋果一樣紅. Don't put 一樣 after the adjective.
A and B can be nouns, verbs, or whole sentences, not only adjectives.
比 compares higher or lower. 像……一樣 shows things are alike.
B2L06-G01-P143: 好 after a verb means the action is done and the result is as it should be.
V好了 means finished and ready. 沒V好 means not finished yet.
V得好 and V不好 say whether you do it well or badly.
To say the result is bad, put 不 right before 好: 學不好. 不學好 means something different.
B2L06-G02-P144: 錯 after a verb means you did the action, but the result was wrong.
V錯了 says you did it wrong. 沒V錯 says you didn't do it wrong.
Put 錯 after the verb, not before it: 聽錯了, not 錯聽了.
Don't add 了 after 沒V錯.
B2L06-G03-P145: 會 after a verb means you gained a skill by learning or being taught.
It is often used with 學 and 教: 學會 means learn how, and 教會 means teach someone how.
學會了 means you already learned it. 學得會 means you are able to learn it.
Put 不 before 會, as in 教不會. The 不 is about the result, not about 教.
B2L06-G04-P145: Use the same question word twice to say the choice has no limit: whatever, whoever, wherever.
The first part sets the condition. The second part, with 就, gives the matching choice.
Both question words must be the same: 想買什麼就買什麼.
With 誰, the second 誰 can also come before 就.
B2L06-G05-P146: 會 shows the speaker believes something will very likely happen.
Put 的 at the end to sound surer and gentler.
A double no like 不會不同意 means 會同意.
B2L06-G06-P147: 等 says the second thing happens only after the first thing has happened.
Put 就 after the second subject and before the action.
Put 不 or 沒 before 等, not before 就. 沒等 means not waiting for it.
B2L06-G07-P153: 才 before a number says the amount is less than the speaker expected.
只 can also mean a small amount, but it goes before a verb, not directly before a number. 才 can.
才 shows it is the speaker's own opinion that the amount is small.
B2L06-G08-P154: 讓 says A is the reason B feels or becomes a certain way.
Put the person who feels right after 讓, then the feeling: 讓我很開心. The cause comes first.
B2L07-G01-P165: 不但 gives one fact, and 還 adds another that is stronger.
Both parts have the same subject, and the second one can be left out.
Add the second fact with 還 or 也, not 但是.
If the subjects are different, leave out 不但 and use 也 in the second part.
B2L07-G02-P166: 一 plus a measure word, then 都 or 也 plus 不 or 沒, means not even one or not at all.
It often sounds exaggerated or surprising.
Don't leave out the measure word after 一.
Use 不, not 沒, before 願意: 一個字都不願意寫.
B2L07-G03-P166: 讓 plus a person plus a verb means let or allow someone to do something.
It is a polite way to ask someone to act. It sounds softer than 叫 or 要 and is not an order.
Put the person right after 讓. Put 了 at the end or after the verb, not after 讓.
This is 讓 for letting or asking, not 讓 for making someone feel something.
B2L07-G04-P167: Add 是 before an adjective like 美 or 漂亮 to confirm it or stress how much.
A degree word can go between 是 and the adjective.
Put 是 after the subject. Don't add it every time: normally say 很漂亮.
B2L07-G05-P168: 光 after a verb means something is used up or eaten up, with none left.
It often goes with 把 and 了, and can sound unhappy or regretful.
Put 光 after the verb: 吃光了, not 光吃了.
Don't use it for homework. Say 寫完, not 寫光.
B2L07-G06-P169: 一點兒 plus 都 or 也 plus 不 or 沒 means not at all.
Put 一點兒 before 都, not after: 一點兒都不甜.
有一點兒 means a little. 一點兒都 with a no word means not at all.
B2L07-G07-P176: 剛 gives the first thing, and 就 gives the second thing that happens right after.
If the second part has a different subject, put it before 就.
Don't add 了 right after the first action. Go straight to 就.
B2L07-G08-P176: 趁 means using a chance, a time, or good weather to do something that helps you.
After it you can use a noun, a verb phrase, or a state word. 著 is optional.
趁 uses a chance. 因為 gives a reason.
Don't say 趁了. Say 趁著 or 趁.
B2L08-G01-P188: 滿 before a number and measure word means that amount is reached.
The next part says what applies once it is reached: 滿十杯就可以替客人送過去.
沒滿十八歲 means not yet eighteen.
B2L08-G02-P188: 連 brings up the most surprising or extreme example. 都 or 也 says it is true even for that.
Put 連 and the example before 都 or 也: 連睡覺的時間都沒有.
For not even one, put 一 and a measure word after 連, then 都 or 也 and 不 or 沒.
都 here doesn't mean all of them.
B2L08-G03-P189: 像 brings up an example, and 這樣 or 那樣 points back to what the example is like.
Add 的 and a noun to name the kind of person, thing, or place that has those features.
Put the example before the kind: 像洗碗筷這樣的家事.
B2L08-G04-P190: 只好 says you have no other choice, so you do the only thing left.
Say the reason or problem first. Put the action after 只好.
只好 shows a choice forced by limits. 可以 only shows ability or permission.
B2L08-G05-P191: 為了 says the purpose of an action.
After it, use a noun phrase or an action. The main action comes after the purpose.
For a cause, use 因為. 為了 gives the goal, not the reason.
B2L08-G06-P197: 上 after a verb can mean putting something on, reaching a goal, or entering a new state.
The verb and the sentence show which meaning it is, as with 穿上 for putting on.
Forms: V上了 means done, 沒V上 not done, V得上 can, and V不上 can't.
B2L08-G07-P198: 因為……的關係 gives a short reason. Use a noun or short phrase, not a full sentence, in the middle.
The reason can come before or after the result.
Don't swap in 為了. 因為 gives the cause, and 為了 gives the purpose.
B2L09-G01-P208: A sentence ending in 嗎 with 不 or 沒 before the verb can be a challenge, not a real question.
The speaker is not asking for information. They treat the fact as already known, so it can sound impolite.
B2L09-G01-P218: Some state words can be doubled to show a high degree: AA for one syllable, AABB for two.
Use 的 when the doubled word describes the subject or a noun after it. Use 地 when it describes a verb.
Doubling already means a high degree, so don't add 很 or 非常.
Not every state word can be doubled.
B2L09-G02-P209: Put 快 before a verb to tell someone to hurry up.
Put 慢 before a verb to ask someone to slow down.
You can add 一 before 點兒 or leave it out.
B2L09-G03-P209: 到 after a verb marks where the action ends: a place, a time, or the end of a range or amount.
For a place, you can add 來 or 去 after it.
For a time, the action goes on until that time.
B2L09-G04-P211: A question word in a negative sentence gives a soft answer that doesn't say much.
It can mean not very, not much, didn't go anywhere, or didn't go with anyone.
B2L09-G05-P212: 怎麼這麼 plus a state word shows surprise or disbelief about a situation.
The speaker is not always waiting for an answer.
B2L09-G06-P212: V得下 and V不下 say whether there is enough room, or enough ability, to fit or finish something.
In this meaning, 下 is used only in these two forms.
B2L10-G01-P231: 不但 and 而且 join two short sentences, and the second one says something even stronger.
If both sentences have the same subject, put it before 不但, and you can leave it out of the second sentence.
If the subjects are different, put one after 不但 and the other after 而且.
B2L10-G01-P239: 對 NP 來說 gives someone's opinion or attitude about a specific event.
Put the person between 對 and 來說, then give the comment.
B2L10-G02-P232: 死了 after a state word exaggerates it, and is stronger than 得不得了 and 極了.
It usually has a negative meaning.
A few state words can show happy feelings, such as 高興死了.
B2L10-G02-P240: 的話 means if, like 如果 and 要是, but it goes at the end of the first part.
如果 and 要是 go at the start. They can be used with 的話, and either one can be left out.
要是 can sound stronger, even threatening, and 的話 is less formal.
B2L10-G03-P232: 越 ... 越 ... says that as the first action grows or shrinks in degree or number, the situation changes with it.
With one subject, put 越 before both verbs.
With two subjects, the second subject's state changes as the first subject does something more.
B2L10-G03-P241: Says the subject, often a thing, helps, influences, or benefits someone or something.
Put 對 and the person or thing first, then 有 or 沒 plus 幫助, 影響 or 好處.
B2L10-G04-P233: 到底 pushes for an answer and shows the speaker is eager to know.
Use it in choice questions like 要不要 or 去不去, or with a question word, but not with 嗎.
It can go before or after the subject, but if the subject is a question word, 到底 goes before it.
B2L11-G01-P250: Place word + verb + 了 or 著 + noun says that something exists in a place.
Posture verbs tell how a person or animal is in that place, such as 坐 and 站.
Other verbs tell how things are put there, such as 放 and 掛.
B2L11-G02-P252: 對 ... 感興趣 says the subject is interested in something and wants to know it better.
Put what you are interested in between 對 and 感興趣. It can be a noun or a verb phrase.
Put 不 before 感興趣 to say not interested.
B2L11-G03-P252: After a verb of the senses like 看 or 聽, 出來 means you can make something out by that sense.
After 想 or an action verb, it means something comes from nothing, so 想出來 means to come up with an idea.
Put 得 or 不 between the verb and 出來 to say you can or can't.
B2L11-G04-P253: 嘛 marks the topic and gives a pause while the speaker thinks about what to say next about it.
Put 嘛 right after the topic, then add the comment.
B2L11-G05-P254: 同 + 一 + a measure word says that different people or things share the same situation.
The shared thing can be the same object, time, location and so on.
A noun can follow the measure word, but it is not required.
B2L11-G06-P260: After a list of examples, 等 can sum them up with a number for the total or a word for the category.
Put 等 at the end of a list to show there are many more of the same kind.
B2L11-G07-P260: 從 ... 中 says someone learns about a situation, deals with something, or gets benefits from something.
In this pattern, 中 means inside, not middle.
B2L12-G01-P271: 除了 means except for. It names what is left out, and 都 comes in the second part.
After 除了 you can use a noun, a verb, or a state verb with no object.
The subject can go before 除了 or before 都.
B2L12-G02-P272: 像 or 不像 compares the first thing with the second. 不像 says the first is not as much as the second.
After 那麼 or 這麼 comes a state verb that shows degree.
B2L12-G03-P273: This pattern says something starts from a certain time or action. 起 means begin.
從 often goes before a time word or verb phrase, and it can be left out.
就 often starts the second part. The subject can go at the start or in the second part.
B2L12-G04-P273: 向 can show the direction of an action. Before a person, it shows who the action is aimed at.
Compared with 跟, 向 sounds more formal, polite and respectful.
B2L12-G05-P274: 難怪 says a result is no surprise, now that you know the reason.
The known fact usually comes first, then 難怪 and the result.
A verb phrase often follows 難怪, and it can also start a reply in conversation.
B2L12-G06-P275: V得了 says you can do the action or reach the result. The negative is V不了.
It often goes with a verb of one syllable.
It is about being able to do it. V了 is different, because it says the action is done.
B2L12-G07-P282: 個 after a verb makes the action sound short, relaxed or easy.
Words made of a verb and its object often use this form, such as 喝個茶.
B2L12-G08-P283: 來 stands in for an action that is already clear from the context, often a specific one.
自己來 is a polite way to say you don't want to trouble someone else.
B2L13-G01-P293: 不管 ... 都 says that in every possible condition, the result stays the same.
After 不管 come the possible conditions, and after 都 comes the situation that does not change.
What follows 不管 is a question: a question word, A-not-A, a choice, or two opposite one-syllable words.
B2L13-G02-P294: 不如 offers a better suggestion than the original action.
Before 不如, the speaker can comment on the original action to explain why.
After the suggestion, you can add a further explanation.
B2L13-G03-P294: 了一點兒 after a state word says something is not as good as expected, but not by much.
It usually shows small weaknesses or a mild complaint, like 貴了一點兒.
B2L13-G04-P301: 比 means than. The thing you compare with goes after it: 我比你高.
比較 means more. The subject goes before it and the state verb goes after it.
比起來 gives a remark about one thing compared with another, often as 跟 B 比起來.
B2L13-G05-P302: 差一點兒 says something almost happened.
It is followed by a verb or verb phrase, and it is usually about something the speaker did not want.
B2L13-G06-P303: 白 plus a verb, often a one-syllable one, says an action was done but did not have the effect it should have.
With verbs like 吃, 喝 and 住, it means not willing to pay money or make effort.
B2L14-G01-P316: 想起來 is used when someone suddenly remembers something almost forgotten, or remembers it with great effort.
想得起來 and 想不起來 say whether someone can remember something almost forgotten or from long ago.
B2L14-G02-P317: 從來 plus 沒 or 不 says someone has never done something, or never does it.
Put 從來 and 沒 or 不 before the verb.
B2L14-G03-P317: 等等 at the end of a list shows there are more items of the same kind that are not listed.
It works like 等. Normally, don't put 等等 after proper nouns.
B2L14-G04-P325: 當 ... 就 says that when one situation happens, another follows right away.
當 is often used with 的時候.
B2L14-G05-P325: 讓 can work like 被, to say what was done to the subject. The doer after 讓 can't be left out.
As a verb, 讓 can mean to cause something to happen, or to make someone feel or do something.
It can also mean to allow someone to do something. Asking someone to do something with 讓 sounds more polite and soft.
B2L14-G06-P327: 無所謂 shows the speaker is indifferent to something or does not care about it.
Put it after the thing, or use it alone.
B2L14-G07-P328: 走 after an action verb means something leaves or disappears.
The verb is an action verb, such as 搬, 拿 or 帶.
Put 得 or 不 between the verb and 走 to say you can or can't.
B2L14-G08-P329: 要不是 is followed by a fact that did happen. Without that fact, something else would have happened.
The second situation did not really happen.
B2L15-G01-P341: 可 adds emphasis to the verb or state verb after it.
It is used to deny someone's opinion, stress a fact, or show that an expected result finally happened.
It can also mean be sure to, or remind someone to do something.
B2L15-G02-P342: A measure word for actions counts how many times an action happens.
Examples of these measure words are 拳, 眼, 口, 次 and 遍.
Put 一 and the measure word after the verb.
B2L15-G03-P343: 下來 after a verb can show an action moving downward.
It can also mean writing something down or buying something, such as 記下來.
It can also mean stopping a movement and staying.
B2L15-G04-P343: 說 V 就 V says you do something right away, without much hesitation or thought.
It can also show that something happens easily or often.
B2L15-G05-P351: 誰知道 says something happened unexpectedly.
Here it is a question that doesn't need an answer. Put the surprising result after it.
B2L16-G01-P361: 得很 shows a high degree. It is more common in conversation, to stress a situation.
It is close in meaning to 死了 and 得不得了, but is often used to show disapproval of someone's opinion.
B2L16-G02-P362: 得看 or 要看 says what someone will do depends on the situation after 看.
After 看 you can have a phrase or noun, such as a question word, A-not-A, or two opposite one-syllable words.
B2L16-G03-P363: 像 ... 什麼的 gives examples to explain further, and shows that the list is long.
Speakers often give only 2 to 3 items because of limited space or time.
B2L16-G04-P364: V 來 V 去 shows an action repeated many times in a short time.
It is used when someone is waiting or walking around.
The two verbs are often the same.
B2L16-G05-P370: A 比得上 B means A can compare with B, or is even better.
A 比不上 B says A can't compare with B.
B2L16-G06-P371: 只有 gives a condition that must be met. The result after 才 happens only if it is met.
